fingerprints.story: The storm had not merely passed; it had been exorcised from the sky, leaving behind a silence so profound it felt like pressure against the eardrums. Elias Thorne stood on the gallery of the Blackwood Point Lighthouse, the salt spray still clinging to his wool coat, his hands trembling not from the cold, but from the weight of the object cradled in his palms. It was a clockwork nightingale, no larger than a sparrow
